- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or neutral (0.00), model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if price is trending down.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >+5% from prior day), model frequently overshoots in next few days; cap forecast at +3–5% above peak.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-period, model often fails to catch the reversal; increase forecast slope gently.
- Mean reversion bias: if price is above 3σ from 30-day mean, model tends to overreact; dampen forecast toward historical mean.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates late-period (last 7–10 days) if sentiment is bullish; add 0.5–1.5% buffer to end of forecast.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “0.67” followed by “0.33”, model tends to overcorrect; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% in next 3–5 days.
